question: Refer to the exhibit. Three operational endpoints are deployed under the same application EPG. Only the ICMP traffic must be permitted within the Web_EPG. Which two actions must be taken to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)
context: Topology: two spines connect to Leaf1-4, which connect to Endpoint2, Endpoint1, Endpoint3, all in EPG: Web_EPG, BD: Web_BD.
imageNote: Diagram: two spines connect to Leaf1-4, which connect to Endpoint2, Endpoint1, Endpoint3 respectively, all in EPG: Web_EPG, BD: Web_BD.
options: Check box of forward control proxy ARP.
Set VRF policy control preference to unenforced.
Add Taboo contract on the Web_EPG.
Configure intra EPG contract under Web_EPG.
Mark intra EPG isolation as enforced.
theory: By default, endpoints within the same EPG can communicate freely without any contract. To restrict that intra-EPG traffic down to only ICMP, you must first mark intra-EPG isolation as Enforced, which blocks all default intra-EPG communication, and then add an explicit intra-EPG contract permitting only ICMP - isolation alone would block everything, while the intra-EPG contract selectively re-opens just the desired protocol between endpoints in the same EPG. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Cisco ACI Contracts and EPG Isolation)
